newsitem.title: USA: US stocks end slightly off but techs still bright.
newsitem.headline: US stocks end slightly off but techs still bright.

text.p: U.S. stocks edged lower as interest-rate caution permeated Wall Street but the renewed leadership of the high-technology sector kept a lid on aggressive selling.

"You have to take your hat off for the market," said Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist of Fahnestock & Co. He said the lack of serious profit-taking "implies the market is not ready to correct despite nervousness, the (recent) sharp run up and next Tuesday's FOMC meeting."
The Dow industrials lost 11 to about 5878.

The blue chip index rallied nearly 230 points last week through Monday amid investor hopes that the Fed would not raise short-term interest rates at next Tuesday's policy meeting. But a Tuesday Reuter report that suggested some Fed members were leaning toward a raise in the 5.0 percent discount rate revived interest rate jitters.
The long bond rose 1/32 to yield 7.02 percent.
Losers outpaced gainers 13-9 on heavy NYSE volume of about 390 million shares.
The Nasdaq Composite, which has surged nearly six percent over the past seven trading sessions, rose two to about 1206.
That brought the tech-studded index closer to June 5's all-time high finish of 1249.15.

Sentiment was aided by Merrill Lynch's naming of International Business Machines its Focus One stock of the week. "I believe my IBM earnings estimates are above consensus for the fourth quarter and if achieved, Wall Street will have greater confidence in 1997 and reward it with a higher P/E," said Daniel Mandresh, Merrill's computer industry analyst.
IBM is expected to Thursday announce a voluntary buyout plan for certain non-strategic and support positions.
Another bellwether, Intel, rose 1-3/8 to 95-5/8.
Intel hit a new 52-week high of 96-1/2 during the day.

Microsoft rose 2-5/8 to 136-1/2, after hitting a year-high 137-7/8. Zona Research, which provides information and advice to the Internet industry, said Microsoft is gaining ground in the Internet browser market against leader Netscape.

Peter Green, a technical analyst at Gruntal & Co, said the broader market has been supported by the technology group's reassertion of leadership. "It's also been helped by hopes interest rates will be left alone."
July trade deficit data further muddied the guesswork on what the Fed would do next week.

The U.S. trade deficit ballooned in July to a surprisingly wide $11.68 billion -- its highest level in more than eight years as imports surged and foreign sales shrank for a second straight month. The data had neglible market impact.
Fahnestock's Barthel said that despite the revived talk of a rate hike, a tightening in the September of a presidential election year has happened only once in the past 90 years, on Sept 26, 1980.
Hildegard Zagorski, Prudential Securities market analyst, said, "The market has been on the defensive and is looking ahead to the Fed meeting."

Among individual stocks, Netscape lost 3-3/8 to 42-5/8. Merrill downgraded the stock, saying Netscape's recent product introductions are "sound first steps, but much more is needed to compete in the long run."

PepsiCo rose 1/2 to 29-1/2 after naming Karl von der Heyden chief financial officer and vice chairman for about one year to help formulate long-term growth strategy and identify a successor. Von der Heyden had been a non-executive director at Cadbury Schweppes and held previous posts at PepsiCo.
Hercules Inc rose 3-1/8 to 55-3/8. Prudential Securities started coverage with a buy.

International Network Services, which provides services for complex enterprise networks, soared 92 percent or 14-3/4 points to 30-3/4 in its Wall Street debut. Cisco Systems has an 8.3 percent stake in the company.

Olsten lost 3-3/4 to 22-7/8 a day after shares of ManPower, the world's largest private employment agency, tumbled after guiding Street estimates slightly lower. Robert W. Baird & Co cut Olsten to moderately attractive from aggressive buy and trimmed 1996 estimates.
Tambrands rose 1-1/8 to 42-7/8 after news of a restructuring. Morgan Stanley and JP Morgan upgraded the stock.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 2.40 to 1205.71.
The S&P 500 index fell 1.47 to 681.47.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk, 212 859 1721
